findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public network endpoint. Although the shown security-group rule limits MySQL ingress to the VPC CIDR, this unnecessarily exposes the database to Internet-reachable attack paths if security-group rules change or other network controls are misconfigured.
The RDS instance explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, so database storage and associated automated backups are not encrypted at rest by RDS.

The EC2 instance role is granted s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on every resource. Compromise of the application instance would grant broad control over S3, EC2, and RDS resources in the account beyond what the application needs.

The database username and plaintext password are rendered into EC2 user data and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data and the resulting credential file can be accessed by principals or processes with instance-level access, increasing the risk of database credential disclosure.

MySQL port 3306 is allowed from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application server security group or specific required clients. Any compromised host or workload in the VPC can attempt to connect to the database.
